title: Runtime environments, engines and connector deployment
intro:
Everything about getting IDMC to actually RUN something: which runtime type to pick, what an engine is versus a licence, where third-party drivers go, and how to size the host. This is the layer that decides whether a perfectly-formed API call does any work, and it is where a whole deployment session was spent learning things no endpoint table would tell you.

The governing idea: **a runtime environment is a NETWORK POSITION, not a setting.** Whatever runs your task must be able to reach your data. Every runtime decision below follows from that one fact.

blocks.title: The three runtime types — pick by where your data lives
rows: Informatica Cloud Hosted Agent
Inside the IDMC hosting facility. Nothing to install.
Source and target are both SaaS and the connector supports it (check the connector's own guide — support is per-connector).
Reach anything on a private network. It is multi-tenant. A connection bound to it CREATES fine and then cannot see a private host — a 200 that means nothing.
Secure Agent group
A host you own and run.
Data is on-premises or on a private network — or SaaS data you do not want going through the Hosted Agent. **The only option that reaches a private database.**
Be avoided if your data is private. You own patching, disk, RAM and uptime.
Serverless runtime environment

Informatica-managed compute **inside YOUR OWN AWS or Azure account** — you supply the VPC/VNet, subnets and an IAM role. Vendor wording: auto-scales with the workload 'while your data remains in your cloud environment'. Single-tenant, dedicated VM resources.
Your data is already in AWS or Azure and you want no agent to maintain.
Reach data in any OTHER cloud or datacentre. It is not a general replacement for a Secure Agent — it is an AWS/Azure-native runtime. Also bills IPUs per runtime-hour where an agent is free.

blocks.title: Licence, assignment, deployment, running — four states people collapse into one
rows: 1. LICENSED
Administrator → Licenses in the UI. There is no licence-inventory API. Privileges are the REST proxy.
Absent from the Licenses page. NOT a 404 from REST — every licence path 404s even when fully licensed.
2. ASSIGNED to an agent
UI: Administrator → Runtime Environments → agent → enable components. **UI-only, no REST verb.** Confirmation string in 53-ui-receipts.
agentEngines[] simply does not contain the engine. A connection test names it exactly: 'No running service found of type <Engine> <ver>.* service for AgentGroup: {reId}'.
3. DEPLOYED / DEPLOYING
GET /api/v2/agent/details/{agentId} -> agentEngines[].agentEngineStatus.status

Status sits at DEPLOYING for many minutes while packages download. Calls keep failing meanwhile, and the engine NAMED in the error changes as each one lands. A moving error is progress, not a new wall.
4. RUNNING and resolvable
Only a PASSING connection test proves this. Nothing else does.

status can read RUNNING in the API while the agent's own log says UNKNOWN and the router still refuses. Under host pressure engines flap RUNNING -> STOPPED. Treat status as a deployment signal, never a completion signal.

blocks.title: Third-party JDBC drivers — where they actually go
rows: Canonical directory for a CCI/JDBC_V2 third-party driver
<agent>/ext/connectors/thirdparty/informatica.jdbc_v2/common/ — Informatica auto-creates it and drops its OWN drivers there (DB2, MSSQL, Oracle), which is how you confirm it is right.
Live 2026-07-26. Two earlier guesses were wrong: ext/jdbc/ and apps/Data_Integration_Server/ext/drivers/ were both ignored by the connector.
CAI / process-engine JDBC driver
<agent>/apps/process-engine/ext — the Secure Agent picks jars up from here if you leave 'JDBC Jar Directory' blank. Otherwise set that field to any directory.
Vendor: IC_July2025_(JDBC)ConnectorGuide, ch.2. You must supply EITHER the jar directory OR the driver class name.
The directory only exists after the engine deploys
Do not pre-stage a driver before the engine lands — the path is created by deployment. Stage it, then restart the connector engine so it scans again.
Live: the driver was invisible until Connector_Service restarted.
Shaded-jar trap (ClickHouse, and any driver with a client split)

The `-all` classifier is NOT necessarily shaded. clickhouse-jdbc 0.6.5 `-all` omits com.clickhouse.client.* and throws NoClassDefFoundError ClickHouseClient. The correct artifact is **-shaded**. Verify with `unzip -l <jar> | grep -c client/` before trusting it.
Live. A wrong download also returned a 554-byte HTML 404 page named .jar — always check the size.
JDBC_V2 sends NO password

The plugin XML declares HASUSERNAME="NO" HASUSERPASSWORD="NO" — there are no credential fields. Credentials in the URL, in userinfo form, or in additionalSecurityProperties were all stripped or ignored; the server saw the username but never a password. Read the plugin XML in downloads/package-JDBC_V2*/package/rdtm/plugins/*.xml — it is the authoritative field list.
Live, proven from both ends: the same URL forms all worked from a plain java -cp test, and ClickHouse's own log showed no-password auth.

blocks.title: Sizing the Secure Agent host — enable only what you need
rows: Engine JVM heap reservations
Enabling ALL services put 23 engines on one host whose -Xmx values summed to ~9.2 GB — more RAM than the 7.8 GiB machine had.
Sum the -Xmx of what you enable BEFORE clicking. Budget >=16 GB once Data Integration is on.
What over-subscription looks like

27 OOM-kill events; the Linux OOM killer killed the co-located analytics database server twice plus the document database; load average 54 on 4 cores; engines flapping RUNNING->STOPPED; root disk 79% -> 95%.
Never co-locate a full engine set with production databases on a small host. Add swap — with none, every spike goes straight to the OOM killer.
Disk appetite
~/infaagent grew to 25 GB, 19 GB of it installer packages under downloads/.
Keep ~20 GB free. Installer dirs under downloads/ do NOT map onto apps/ names, so they cannot be safely bulk-deleted by name match mid-deployment.
A governance-only engine set
Data_Integration_Server + Connector_Service + Metadata_Foundation_Agent + Metadata_Platform_Service ran fine (8 engines, 6 RUNNING) after trimming; load fell 65 -> 14.

Untick the rest: At_Scale_Server, B2BProcessor, CIHProcessor, DVProcessor, Database_Ingestion, MassIngestionRuntime, PC2CDI_Modernization_App, Streaming_Ingestion_Agent, ApiMicrogatewayService, AIAgentRuntime, DAM x2.

notes.label: Read the plugin XML, not the guesswork
notes.text: Every CCI connector ships a plugin XML under downloads/package-<CONNECTOR>*/package/rdtm/plugins/. It declares the exact connection attributes, including HASUSERNAME / HASUSERPASSWORD. When a connection keeps failing on credentials, that file settles in seconds what hours of body-shape guessing cannot.

notes.label: Diagnose from BOTH ends
notes.text: The JDBC_V2 credential finding only became provable by testing the same URL from a plain `java -cp <driver> ...` on the agent host (all three credential forms worked) and then reading the database's own auth error (no password presented). When an API error is ambiguous, reproduce the operation outside IDMC — that separates 'the platform will not do it' from 'my body is wrong'.

notes.label: Serverless is not an agent replacement
notes.text: It is compute in YOUR cloud account, so it inherits your cloud's network reachability. If the data is not in that same AWS/Azure network, serverless cannot see it, and a connection bound to it will create with 200 and then fail every test. Also: no REST plane — /public/core/v3/serverlessRuntimeEnvironments and /api/v2/serverlessRuntimeEnvironment both 404 while the control path proves the plane is real, so creation is UI-only.

open_questions: Does any documented mechanism let JDBC_V2 pass a password, or is server-side auth configuration always required for a driver whose plugin declares HASUSERPASSWORD=NO?
Vendor hardware sizing for a Secure Agent by engine set is not in the doc set held here — the >=16 GB figure is inferred from observed -Xmx totals, not published guidance.
